newsitem.title: USA: Maxxam shareholders lose redwood vote despite protests.
newsitem.headline: Maxxam shareholders lose redwood vote despite protests.

text.p: Environmental protesters sang, shouted and offered a $25,000 reward for the arrest of Maxxam Inc. Chairman Charles Hurwitz Thursday, but lost a vote calling for the company to sell 60,000 acres of California redwood forests.
The resolution, put forth at the Maxxam annual meeting by shareholders who want to protect the ancient trees, was voted down by a margin of 98.4 percent to 1.45 percent.
Because of a heavy proxy vote, the returns were not complete, but Maxxam general counsel Byron Wade said the remaining ballots were too few to change the outcome.
The resolution's defeat was expected because Hurwitz and his family own 61 percent of Houston-based Maxxam.

The company opposed the proposal because it said it could undermine a still-pending agreement to swap Maxxam's most coveted redwood grove, the 5,600-acre Headwaters Forest, for government land and $300 million in cash and considerations.

Environmentalists said selling the 60,000-acre forest, or swapping it to get rid of possible liabilities tied to the 1988 collapse of a Texas thrift run by Hurwitz, would improve the company's financial performance.
"You have an albatross around your neck ... it drags your company down," said shareholder David Shernoff.
Investor George Ireland disagreed. Selling off the land "guts (Maxxam unit) Pacific Lumber as a viable operating company," he said.
He also chastised Hurwitz for getting too little in the proposed deal for the Headwaters tract.
"We thought Headwaters was worth substantially more. We think you're giving it away," he said.

Shareholder representative Ellen Fred, who sang an ode to the trees and animals in the forest, urged Hurwitz to "do the right thing" and save the redwoods. "Who will teach the young owls to fly?" she sang.
"You have a beautiful voice," a smiling Hurwitz told her.
Darryl Cherney of environmental group Earth First told Hurwitz: "I have quietly acquired five shares (in Maxxam) and it is my intention to take over your company."
He then announced a $25,000 reward for "information leading to the arrest, conviction and jailing of corporate raider Charles Hurwitz."
Outside the meeting, Greenpeace activists shouted "Save the redwoods, Jail Hurwitz" and inflated a giant ballon in the shape of a chainsaw.
Hurwitz told shareholders he was doing what was best for the company. "We pay taxes on those trees. We should be entitled to cut them or be compensated for them," he said.
He told Reuters he was not worried that Maxxam's image was suffering from the redwoods controversy.
"What do you do? You have something -- either you get no value or you get some value from it," he said.
